sprint: Image Studio rebrand + Turn/Flip transforms (Feature 1 Phase 1)
task: User-visible strings across index.html/app.js/buildInfo.js swapped from 'Drawing Magic'/'My Drawing'/'Magic Drawing' vocabulary to 'Image Studio'/'Before'/'After'/'Original'/'Edited' — the tool is now a generic image editor's name in the UI while every internal identifier (file path 'tools/background-remover/', class 'new-drawing-btn', DOM ids '#magicOverlay'/'#magicMessage'/etc., function names) stays completely unchanged per explicit direction ('renaming not required'). New Turn/Flip capability added: 'js/transform.js' is a new DOM-free pure pixel-buffer transform module (rotate90/rotate270/flipHorizontal/flipVertical, each taking and returning a {data:Uint8ClampedArray, width, height} shape, leaving the input untouched so upstream state — original buffer, undo snapshots — can be preserved by the caller). Wired into 'app.js' via a Turn/Flip tool (accessed via a new 'Turn / Flip' tile in the tool grid, opening a sub-panel with four choices: Turn Left / Turn Right / Flip ↔ / Flip ↕). Transforms operate on workingBuffer (post-background-removal) rather than the originalPixelBuffer so they run after removal — same pattern as applyManualCrop() already established. Cleanup history is invalidated on every transform since geometry changed. Verified end-to-end via Playwright with a real 4-quadrant coloured test PNG (TL=red, TR=green, BL=blue, BR=yellow): drove Welcome→Magic→Result→'Make It Better'→Edit view, exercised all four operations in sequence, sampled pixels at TL/TR/BL/BR after each — Turn Left rotated 90° CCW (TL green, TR yellow, BL red, BR blue), Flip Horizontal mirrored X (TL yellow, TR green, BL blue, BR red), Turn Right rotated 90° CW (TL blue, TR yellow, BL red, BR green), Flip Vertical mirrored Y and combined with the earlier three returned to the original quadrant layout (TL red, TR green, BL blue, BR yellow). Zero console/page errors throughout. No architecture change beyond adding one new transform module and one new tool dispatch; confined to tools/background-remover/.
